- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust downward; apply mean reversion bias toward 1–2% below recent high.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 1–2%.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model exhibits lag; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and reduce amplitude by 1–3%.
- If true outcome shows rapid downward trend after a high, model often fails to recognize it; apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 3–5 days if sentiment drops below 0.50.
